question: Who said, "A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Macaulay**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Macaulay** made the statement, "**A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia**."
 
• Thomas Babington Macaulay was a British historian and politician.
 
• He is known for his work in promoting English education in India during the British colonial period.
 
• His views on Indian and Arabian literature were part of his broader argument for the introduction of English as the medium of instruction in Indian schools and colleges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Thomas Macaulay was instrumental in drafting the Indian Penal Code, which still forms the backbone of criminal law in India and Pakistan.
 
• His Minute on Indian Education in 1835 laid the foundation for the British educational policy in India.
 
• Despite his contributions, Macaulay's views have been criticized for being Eurocentric and dismissive of the rich literary traditions of India and Arabia.
 
• Macaulay's legacy in India is a subject of debate, with opinions divided on the impact of his policies on Indian society and culture.
